title: How One Thought Changes Across Languages
production_path_basis: Roles, reordering, morphology, and the reading sequence must remain understandable without audio.
central_message: English and Uzbek can package one intended event with different neutral orders and grammatical signals while preserving recognizable semantic roles.
takeaway: Grammar reorganizes and marks meaning; a gloss explains structure but is not itself a natural translation.
platform: website showcase and bundled desktop example
language: English interface with English and standard Uzbek examples
linguistic_depth: semantic roles, neutral SVO/SOV contrast, definite accusative -ni, progressive -yap, third-person form, and variation boundary
visual_direction: dark token-transform storyboard with stable role colors and explicit morpheme decomposition
pacing: meaning, reorder, compare, morphology, timed reading path, variation boundary
constraints: do not imply literal one-to-one translation
do not generalize one neutral order to every utterance
success_criteria: English and Uzbek orders remain directly comparable
the reading path is addressable and timed
variation and audio limitations remain explicit
